'''''Mammillaria compressa''''', commonly called '''mother of hundreds''', is a species of [[cactus]] in the subfamily [[Cactoideae]].<ref name="Wiersema">{{cite book |last1=Wiersema |first1=John H. |last2=León |first2=Blanca |title=World Economic Plants: A Standard Reference, Second Edition |publisher=CRC Press |year=2016 |location=Boca Raton |isbn=978-1466576810 |page=431 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=AIrNBQAAQBAJ&q=%22Mammillaria+compressa%22&pg=PA431 |access-date=17 February 2020 |via=GoogleBooks}}</ref> It is native to northern and southern Mexico, and is cultivated as an ornamental plant.<ref name="Wiersema" /> It blooms in the winter and early spring, with bell-shaped flowers that range from a purplish pink to red color.<ref name="LLIFLE">{{cite web |title=Mammillaria compressa |url=http://www.llifle.com/Encyclopedia/CACTI/Family/Cactaceae/11897/Mammillaria_compressa |website=LLIFLE |date=14 November 2005 |access-date=17 February 2020}}</ref> Its curved spines were traditionally used as hooks for fishing.<ref name="LLIFLE"/>
